answer: Sequential certification gates fake identities. A new identity climbs three rungs: a basic task, a paid task, and a reviewed task, each checked by a different verifier with one epoch between rungs. Each rung ends with an echo check. The verifier replays the work against the log and stamps an opal seal. Each extra identity costs 3 tasks at 20 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 60,000 credits with no shortcut. The named failure mode is ladder rental: a rented account fails because rung history binds to the key and transfer resets it. An honest agent pays once and earns a nectar share.
